pay_reaching_households.label: Pay reaching households
pay_reaching_households.description: A broad income-per-person proxy: it does not measure wages, take-home pay, inequality, or household disposable income.
pay_reaching_households.source_label: GNI per capita, Atlas method (current US$)

cost_of_staying_alive.label: Cost of staying alive
cost_of_staying_alive.description: Annual consumer-price pressure proxy: it is not a rent, food, energy, or household-cost-burden measure.

breathing_room_debt.label: Breathing room / debt pressure
breathing_room_debt.description: Private-credit-stock proxy, not household debt, debt service, delinquency, savings, or credit access. Higher credit can reflect access as well as exposure.
breathing_room_debt.source_label: Domestic credit to private sector (% of GDP)

labor_leverage.label: Labor leverage
labor_leverage.description: Employment attachment proxy, not bargaining power, wages, job quality, union density, hours, or worker protections.
labor_leverage.source_label: Employment-to-population ratio, ages 15+, total (%) (modeled ILO estimate)

customer_cash.label: Customer cash / spending capacity
customer_cash.description: Household/NPISH consumption per-person proxy: it is spending, not cash balances, disposable income, consumer credit, or purchasing-power parity.
customer_cash.source_label: Households and NPISHs final consumption expenditure per capita (constant 2015 US$)

household_circulation_v2.rule: A score is published only when all five source readings are available. Missing data is not imputed. The pipeline uses World Bank primary series, documented same-family WDI fallbacks, then named IMF international fallbacks where WDI has no coverage. Each observed reading retains its source, series, URL, and observation year; a stale Iranian 2018 credit observation is explicitly labeled in its source record.
household_circulation_v2.warning: This is a provisional source-backed model, not a verdict on whether people in a country are doing well. It lacks globally comparable rent burden, household debt-service, disposable-income, wage, underemployment, and multiple-jobholding data.
